llm.summary: The skill is coherent and not malicious, but it gives agents broad persistence, logging, background monitoring, and skill-patching instructions without enough user control or data-handling limits.

dimensions.detail: The optional guardian cron job is a recurring background monitor that reads session state and logs reports, which is related to the purpose but needs clearer setup, containment, and opt-in boundaries.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Installation is a normal skill copy plus an optional executable Python helper and optional cron template; the package does not hide an installer or automatic post-install execution.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Several mitigations tell the agent to act directly rather than ask first, including persisting all critical facts, writing session summaries to memory or a file, spawning isolated subagents, and patching stale skills immediately.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill encourages memory writes and file logging of session-derived facts and cognitive-state reports without retention, permission, redaction, or secret-handling limits; the heuristics even include passwords, tokens, and credentials as memory-debt candidates.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose, agent self-monitoring for context fatigue, attention drift, memory debt, confidence erosion, fragmentation, and skill staleness, matches most of the guidance and the self_check.py utility.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review this skill before installing in environments with sensitive chats, shared machines, or autonomous agents. If used, require explicit user approval before memory writes, file logging, cron deployment, subagent delegation, or skill patching; also redact secrets and set retention and file-permission limits for any logs.
llm.findings:
[SDI-2] unexpected: The artifact really does instruct the agent to patch stale skills immediately. Skill maintenance is related to staleness recovery, but direct modification of skill files without explicit user approval is broader than monitoring/reporting.
[SQP-2] expected: The SKILL.md passive logging example appends cognitive-state records to a predictable home-directory log. Logging is expected for this purpose, but the artifact lacks permission, retention, and sensitivity guidance.
[SQP-2] expected: The guardian cron template explicitly logs full reports to a file. This is disclosed and purpose-aligned, but it persists operational metadata without rotation, access-control, or minimization guidance.
[RA2] expected: Persisting critical facts and session summaries is coherent with context-fatigue recovery, but the instruction is broad and does not require consent, scope limits, or exclusion of secrets before writing to memory or files.
